summary.name: Mole
summary.one_liner: Mole is a native macOS app (and open-source CLI) that cleans caches and AI tool leftovers, uninstalls and updates apps, analyzes disk usage, maintains the system, and shows live system stats.
use_cases: Clearing caches and junk files to free disk space
Uninstalling apps along with their leftover files
Finding the largest files and folders on a disk
Cleaning old sessions and caches from AI coding tools
Monitoring CPU, memory, GPU, disk, network and temperature
summary.what_it_does: Mole is a native Mac app that reviews and cleans caches, logs and leftover data, including caches and old versions from AI tools such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. It uninstalls apps with their leftovers reviewed together and can check updates from Sparkle, the App Store, Homebrew and other supported sources. A whole-disk treemap lets you drill into folders, and deletions go to the Trash where they can be restored. It also shows live CPU, memory, GPU, disk, network, temperature and fan metrics, process details, and can display chosen metrics in the menu bar. The page states scans and cleanup stay on the Mac and files are never uploaded.
notable: Cleanup, app uninstaller, disk analyzer and live system monitor combined in one app
Reviews each item before cleaning; system folders are view-only and Trash items ask before permanent deletion
AI tool data review for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar tools
caveats: The desktop app is a paid product; comments mention a one-time purchase, but the page itself does not state prices
Scope is macOS only, per the page
Some comments mention the CLI is free and open source, but the desktop app is distinct from it
